name: Korrath
description: Korrath is a dual-action compound that simultaneously floods the limbic system with a proprietary synthetic norepinephrine analogue while suppressing prefrontal cortical activity, producing a state of extreme aggression, pain indifference, and total commitment to offensive action. Nightshade markets it legally as an 'extreme sport performance compound' with a thin disclaimer about recreational use, but its combat applications are the entire point. Users in the grip of Korrath do not retreat, do not hesitate, and do not stop.
effects: Extreme aggression and loss of hesitation or restraint
Near-total pain indifference through limbic override
Massively elevated physical output — strength and speed at physiological maximum
Tunnel-vision focus on immediate physical threat elimination
Immunity to morale-breaking stimuli — fear, horror, screaming
side_effects: Complete loss of tactical judgment and threat prioritization
Inability to distinguish ally from enemy in chaotic environments
Rhabdomyolysis from pushing muscles past safe limits
Post-duration crash involving profound depression and dissociation lasting 24-48 hours
Memory fragmentation or blackout during peak effect
Cumulative neurological damage to prefrontal cortex with repeated use
Rare cases of permanent personality change after heavy use
cultural_context: Korrath is what you take when you're outnumbered and you've decided that surviving the next five minutes is more important than making decisions in the five minutes after that. On the Shelf, Korrath users are feared and pitied in equal measure — the drug works, but the people who use it regularly become hollow. Shelf gangs sometimes force-dose captured enemies with Korrath to watch them turn on each other. There's a Korrath subculture in underground fighting rings where promoters pair two dosed fighters and sell footage of the result.
story_hooks: A runner's close ally went into a building dosed on Korrath three days ago and hasn't come out — the building is now a scene of unexplained carnage and the ally is somewhere inside, possibly still under the drug's influence.
Nightshade has a new Korrath formulation with a longer duration and improved target discrimination — they're looking for test subjects who won't be missed.

A Shelf community leader is trying to organize a Korrath buyback and treatment program for former users, but the supplier keeps finding new distribution channels — and the supplier may have Tier 4 backing.
